what_this_is: A finding, not a strike. Every kept M source was judged by the words it defines; the method's own critic found it unable to see a Harkavy-class leak; the decisive test was then run over the whole store and is recorded here with its numbers. Nothing in the store changed on the strength of this record. A ruling on the residue is the owner's.

review.method: one judge per source over a sample of up to sixty routes spread evenly across the source's contribution; three refuters (orthography, provenance, definitions) on every flag, one refuter on every clearance below high confidence; a completeness critic over the whole
critic_gaps: DETECTION POWER: 60 routes against N. For every source with more than ~1,200 routes the sample is under 5% and P(a 1% contamination leaves no trace in 60 draws) = 0.99^60 = 55%; P(miss 5%) = 5%. The Harkavy damage that started this was 376 readings on 252 keys = 0.05% of the store; a contamination of that size inside M14 (148,076 routes, sample 0.04%), M4 (95,089), M25 (72,063), M3, M21, M11, M9, M6, M20, M18, M13, M5, M17, M15 or M1 is invisible to this method by construction.

KEY-SIDE CUES CANNOT FIRE: a full pass over all 124,935 keys finds 2,554 with any mark in U+05B0-U+05C7, nearly all maqaf, and ZERO keys carrying אַ אָ ײ ױ ײַ. Keys are consonant-stripped, and Harkavy's keys were unpointed anyway. The brief's Yiddish vowel-letter and ligature cues are therefore unavailable; only consonant shapes (וו, יי, ע as e) and the English gloss remain, and the doubled-וו/יי shape is also produced legitimately by Hebrew full spelling (M44, M68, M85, M95, M116 are 25-40% such keys).

ETYMOLOGY AND DIALECT TAGS ARE NOT IN THE STORE: rows carry [rank, gloss, fuller gloss, M, year]. Kaikki/Wiktionary etymology ('from Yiddish', 'from Arabic') and Aramaic dialect labels (Classical Syriac, Jewish Babylonian Aramaic, Christian Palestinian Aramaic, Samaritan) are not shipped, so the brief's 'definition describes a Yiddish/Arabic word' cue and any Syriac/Mandaic discrimination inside 'Aramaic' cannot be read from a sample of what the store holds.

FOUND AND CLEARED ANYWAY - M6 MUSE: Yiddish function words are keys with transliterations as definitions: וואס => wass, ווייל => wale, גאר => gar, הייס => hayes, גלאט => glatt, וואו => whoa, שיין => shane, פאלק => falk, מאזל => maazel, ביסל => bissell. M6 has 1,795 keys with doubled וו/יי out of 23,065 routes; the 60-sample saw only transliterated surnames and passed it HEBREW(high). MUSE is an induced alignment lexicon whose 'Hebrew' side is whatever Hebrew-script string occurred in the corpus; it is not a dictionary of anything.

FOUND AND CLEARED ANYWAY - M60 Kaikki Aramaic: Classical Syriac Christian senses served under Hebrew-script keys: מריא => 'Lord; the Christian concept of God and Jesus', צליבא => crucifix, עדתא => church, משיחתא => 'Messiah, Christ', שמשא => 'minister, deacon', כפורא => 'unbeliever, infidel'. English Wiktionary's 'Aramaic' header merges JBA, Syriac, CPA and Samaritan; the label 'Aramaic' admits all of it. Same extractor feeds M72 and M177.

FOUND AND CLEARED ANYWAY - Yiddish lexemes as keys in open-vocabulary aggregators: M15 שטעטל, מענטש, קוויטלעך, קוגל, שנאפס, שמוק, שיין (=>Shayne), ביסל (=>Bissell); M1 שטעטל, קניידלעך; M21 קניידלעך => Klöße, לאטקעס => latke; M22/M43 לאטקעס. Whether these are Hebrew loan usage or Yiddish headwords cannot be decided from the gloss; the source's own marking is what decides it and it is not in the store.

PROVENANCE UNREADABLE FROM THIS CHECKOUT: every ledgers/work/ldmprs/source-cache/... and definition-poc/... pointer is absent from the tree. So it cannot be verified whether the Hebrew Wiktionary extractors (M27 M29 M38 M54 M55 M59 and the inflection/full-spelling/heading-alternate siblings) filtered by the page's language section - he.wiktionary hosts Yiddish, Aramaic, Ladino and Judeo-Arabic entries under Hebrew-script titles - nor whether the Wikidata extractors (M10 M28 M48 M53 M138 and the sense-gloss set M2 M61 M73 M76 M81 M87 M94) filtered on lexeme language rather than script.

INTERLEAVING TEST NOT RUN: the decisive check is kept-store keys INTERSECT Yiddish headwords MINUS Hebrew headwords (Kaikki Yiddish, the struck M40/M63/M104/M168 key sets, Harkavy's key set). None of that data is in the tree and kaikki.org is refused by the proxy (403 on CONNECT). A sample of 60 cannot substitute for this join.

NO KEY-LEVEL / SERVED-POSITION LENS: Harkavy was caught because לענין and דעם were tapped on live books. The sweep judged sources, never keys; nothing asked which kept-source routes actually land on tapped positions in the 3,065 books, or which tapped tokens are Yiddish-shaped and get their only route from an open-vocabulary aggregator (M1 M6 M15 M21 M22 M32 M42 M43 M62).

ZERO-ROUTE CLEARANCES: 25 sources with routes=0 are marked CLEAR. That is a clearance of nothing; if a rebuild re-populates them the verdict will be read as standing. Seven of them (M47 M70 M147 M166 M178 M186 M194) carry medium confidence and the other eighteen high, on identical evidence (none) - the confidence field is not tracking anything.

SAME EXTRACTOR, INDEPENDENT VERDICTS: one hewiktionary_hebrew_exact_english_translation key is split into six M records by year (M27 M29 M38 M54 M55 M59), the inflection extractor into ~15, Wikidata into four. Each got its own 60-sample and verdict; a filter fault in the extractor is shared by all of them, and no lens aggregated across the split.

TRANSLITERATION IS NOT A DEFINITION: M6/M62 rows like סער => sturm, מען => wac, דובער => dovber, סייען => sayan are neither English definitions nor evidence of the headword's language. The sweep only asked 'is the key Hebrew', never 'is the text a definition of it', so a Yiddish key with a Latin transliteration passes both the language lens and the content lens.
critic_method_faults: The sampler's power is fixed at 60 regardless of N, so the method has the same blind spot on a 148,076-route source as on a 2,000-route one; it should scale to a target contamination rate, or better, replace sampling with a full-store pass on the cue set (a full pass over 676,463 routes takes seconds and was done here).

The cue list assumes data the store does not carry: keys are consonant-only (no אַ אָ ײ ױ anywhere), rows carry no etymology and no dialect tag, so the two strongest cues in the brief cannot be observed from the route store at all; the method treats their absence as evidence of absence.

The label test admits 'Hebrew' as the name of an EDITION or PROJECT (Hebrew Wiktionary, Hebrew Wikipedia, Hebrew WordNet) as if it named the headword language - the same shape as Harkavy's 'Hebrew-English', where 'Hebrew' named a target column, not the headwords.

The brief and the enforced rule contradict each other on Syriac: the brief says 'Syriac written in Hebrew script is Aramaic', strike-language-v1.mjs says the owner ruled Syriac and Mandaic out; M60/M72/M177 admit Wiktionary's pan-dialect 'Aramaic' and serve Classical Syriac Christian senses under Hebrew-script keys. One ruling has to give before those three can be judged.

Sources cut from one extractor by year are judged as independent sources; a fault in the extractor is shared and should be judged once across the union, with the union's route count setting the sample.
'CLEAR' is issued on zero evidence for 25 zero-route sources, with two different confidence levels on identical (empty) evidence; a source with no routes should be marked NOT JUDGED, not cleared.

Refutation was applied to flags only, never to clearances: three lenses refuted every flag, but no lens attempted to refute a clearance (e.g. by running the cues over the whole source, or by intersecting with a Yiddish headword list). A method whose only adversarial pressure points toward 'clear' will converge on 'clear'.

The method judges the headword's language but not whether the text is a definition: M6/M62 transliterations (wass, gar, sturm, wac) pass because the key looks Hebrew-script and the text is Latin letters; a transliteration is evidence of neither language nor meaning.

The sweep works per source, not per served position; the failure it is meant to prevent was detected at served positions on live books, and no lens looked at which kept routes actually land on tapped Yiddish-shaped tokens.

Provenance pointers are treated as facts (rule 0) but point at files outside the shipped tree; the method never confirms a pointer resolves, so 'provenance outranks label' currently outranks by name only.
critic_reread: M6 - read every key with doubled וו/יי (1,795) and every key matching Yiddish consonant shapes (וואס ווייל גאר הייס גלאט וואו שיין פאלק מאזל ביסל already confirmed); expect a struck-or-partitioned outcome, not a clearance
M62 - same extractor as M6 (148 doubled-וו/יי keys of 1,449); read all of them

M60 - read every route whose gloss carries Christian/Syriac vocabulary (church, deacon, crucifix, Christ, Lord, monk, baptism, bishop) and reconcile with the owner's Syriac/Mandaic ruling; the store carries no dialect tag so the Wiktionary entry itself must be consulted for each
M72 and M177 - same Kaikki Aramaic extractor as M60; read all 498 and 14 routes for Syriac-only senses

M15 - read the 34 ע-Germanic-shaped keys (שטעטל מענטש קוויטלעך געגוע etc.) and the 891 doubled-וו/יי keys; decide whether a Hebrew Wikipedia article ABOUT a Yiddish word is Hebrew usage under the frame
M1 - read the 522 doubled-וו/יי keys and every edge tagged 'wikt' or 'wp' (ConceptNet /c/he/ ingests translation tables whose language tagging is by script); שטעטל, קניידלעך already present

M21 and M42 - read the 878 and 370 doubled-וו/יי keys; PanLex's Hebrew-script-language partitions M24/M82 were struck, so confirm the 'heb' partition holds no Yiddish (ydd) or Judeo-Arabic expressions that share a spelling; קניידלעך => Klöße and לאטקעס already present
M32 - 278 doubled-וו/יי keys of 5,363; OmegaWiki language tagging is per DefinedMeaning and needs checking on those keys

M27 M29 M38 M54 M55 M59 and all hewiktionary inflection/full-spelling/heading-alternate/recovery siblings (M36 M41 M44 M58 M68 M71 M74 M85 M86 M92 M95 M96 M98 M102 M105 M110 M111 M116 M123 M128 M129 M130 M132 M133 M135 M137 M139 M142 M144 M145 M148-M152 M154 M155 M157 M160-M165 M167 M169-M171 M173 M174 M179 M180 M182 M183 M185 M187-M189 M191 M192 M195) - obtain the extractor manifest and confirm it selects the Hebrew language section of each page, not the page title's script; then read the keys the sweep passed as loans (צימעס קוגל שמוק שלימזל מכללא) to see how he.wiktionary itself marks them
M10 M28 M48 M53 M138 M2 M61 M73 M76 M81 M87 M94 - confirm the Wikidata query filtered lexeme language = Hebrew (Q9288) and not script; M28 carries שלימזל, M10 carries ווי
M25 M11 M13 M50 M69 - Kaikki Hebrew at 0.08-1.6% sample; read all keys with Germanic ע-shapes (געגוע- family is Hebrew, but check געגוען, אבער, איך, מעגליך which the scan flagged)

M46 - the sweep called it HEBREW while M5 and M20 (same BDB) got HEBREW_AND_ARAMAIC: read its Aramaic section to confirm the sample simply missed an 8-10% sub-population, which is the direct measure of what this sampler cannot see

M14 M4 M3 - 0.04-0.14% samples; low language risk because the key set is a closed Biblical form list, but confirm that the key set is in fact bounded to the BHS/Strong's form inventory and carries no open-vocabulary joins
M97 - labeled 'Hebrew and Chaldee' yet passed as HEBREW; 44 keys, read all 85 routes

decisive_test.what: kept-source keys that a struck Yiddish lexicon knows and no curated Hebrew or Aramaic source carries, from aggregator sources only; curated means the compiler tagged the headword's language, aggregator means an alignment product that tags by script

yiddish_headwords.recovered_from: reader/data/route-store at commit c0c19b5ed5d49db3321c0cb3a568ab0fbcb2509e, the store as it stood before the first strike, sources M40 M63 M104 M168 (Kaikki Yiddish) and the twelve Harkavy shards

prefixed_hebrew.note: a clitic letter stripped leaves a curated Hebrew key; these are Hebrew words the curated set lacks in their prefixed form, and they stay

routes.text: To inhale smoke from for example a cigarette or a cigar.

romanized_only.note: every route on the key merely romanizes it — Yiddish function words glossed by their German cognate, Ashkenazi names glossed by their spelling. Not a definition of anything. The narrow strike candidate.

unknown_with_english_gloss.note: a Yiddish lexicon knows the key, no curated source carries it, and the gloss is English. Most are ordinary Hebrew the curated set happens to lack; a few are Yiddish. Separating them needs a Yiddish headword ruling, not a rule.

what_this_does_not_say: that any source is clean. It says the label rule strikes what it can see, the review could not see past it, and the decisive test found a residue of a known size in known places. It also does not say Syriac: three Kaikki Aramaic sources serve Classical Syriac senses under the Wiktionary umbrella of Aramaic, the admission rule names Syriac as struck, and the store carries no dialect tag to separate them; that is a ruling, recorded here as open.
